title: The Accra Bedroom Where Herman Chinery-Hesse Wrote Software on the Bed
conflicts: First contract: a Ghanaian travel firm (WIPO Magazine 2005; Daily Maverick 2011 says early programs were for travel) versus a $5,000 chicken-farm inventory job (Moguldom 2013); the story gives the travel firm as first and the chicken farm as an early job he recalled later. Work in Britain: software developer (WIPO) versus manufacturing engineer (Daily Maverick); reconciled as an engineer who also wrote software freelance. Staff: over 70 staff and 250 clients in 2005 (WIPO) versus 80 staff and over $1m revenue at a 2003 peak (2008 profile quoted by the Ghanaian Times); WIPO's dated 2005 figures used. Premises after the bedroom: outbuildings (Daily Maverick) versus garage (HumanIPO); his own Daily Maverick account used.
notes: Chinery-Hesse died on 16 September 2024; the story says so in its last line. The company field was simplified to 'SOFTtribe (earlier S.O.F.T.)' because a longer form tripped the repeat screen on shared words. Stance 'complicates' (Bacon on what to show and when).
